messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High queue growth / autoscaler fail in azure-southeastasia. Autoscaler error: AllocationDenied - 'Quota limit reached for target SKUs'. Queue depth spike: 220 -> 4,200 in 9m. p95/p99 latency -> 1.2s / 3.8s. Several clients receiving 503s. Severity: P1. Paging @oncall.
tara_oncall: Ack. I'm on it, jumping into the bridge. tagging infra + runtime. @mike_sre can you grab autoscaler logs? @liam_infra pls check Azure quota state.
mike_sre: Looking at autoscaler logs now. Seeing repeated failures:
```
2026-03-15T01:22:13Z ERROR autoscaler: allocation failed: AllocationDenied(ErrorCode=QuotaExceeded, details={"requested":8,"limit":16,"current":16})
2026-03-15T01:22:14Z WARN  autoscaler: retrying allocation after backoff
2026-03-15T01:22:19Z ERROR autoscaler: allocation failed: allocation attempts exhausted
```
Also queue backlog backlog_worker is backpressure'ing workers; continuous-batching backlog rising.
liam_infra: Confirmed quota/limits at subscription level. Running quick az snippet:
```
az vm list-usage --location southeastasia --query "[?name.value=='Standard_NP6_GA...']"
name: "GPUs (N-series)"
limit: 16
currentValue: 16
```
Support portal shows quota increase requests take hours -> days in this subscription. No immediate quota fast-track.
anya_runtime: If quota can't be bumped quickly, we should immediate-fallback to alternate region and/or shrink batch sizes. Proposals:
- 10% traffic -> us-east1 (warm pool) canary
- Evict non-prod GPU pools in southeastasia to free up ~4 GPUs (runbook allows temporary dev eviction)
- Disable large-batch aggregation for 15m to reduce per-request allocation pressure
josh_cs: Heads-up: AcmeCorp and FizzApp already filed tickets reporting timeouts. Acme is on a paid SLA. Need an ETA we can send.
tara_oncall: Doing steps now. Priorities:
1) Route override: canary 10% -> us-east1 (deploy will tag requests with header X-RW-FALLBACK:us-east1)
2) Evict non-prod pools in southeastasia (liam: can you confirm which pools we can drain safely?)
3) Open channel with support to request quota emergency; but plan for fallback since that might not be fast.
liam_infra: Non-prod GPU pools: dev-gpu-1, canary-gpu-2. We can drain dev-gpu-1 for ~6 GPUs. I'm starting the drain script now (will reprovision to non-GPU nodes). Command:
```
./scripts/drain-pool --pool dev-gpu-1 --mode immediate --owner infra
```
This should free 6 GPUs in ~2-3min as containers reschedule. Will post when done.
deploy-bot: canary route override applied by tara_oncall. policy: 10% -> us-east1, all else remain southeastasia. commit abc123 -> roll 10%.
mike_sre: Observing autoscaler after drain start: allocation requests decreased. Backlog ticks down slightly. Queue depth: 4,200 -> 1,150 in 8m. Errors still present for some origins (batch allocations still failing intermittently).
anya_runtime: I'm pushing a runtime toggle to reduce continuous-batching window and disable prefix batching for the next 20m to reduce memory/KV allocation pressure. Will monitor quality regressions.
liam_infra: Drained dev-gpu-1 completed. Freed 6 GPUs. Azure still enforces subscription-per-region quota but freed GPUs via dealloc/reassign means we can satisfy some requests immediately.
tara_oncall: Good. Next: manual scale-up of warmpool in southeastasia using freed capacity + routing to rehydrate active workers. @emma_product want to prep quick customer note.
emma_product: Drafting a short note: "We are experiencing degraded performance in Southeast Asia due to GPU quota limits. We've routed a portion of traffic to alternate region and freed capacity by draining non-prod. Our team is working on full recovery; anticipated gradual improvement over 1-2 hours. We'll follow up with timeline and postmortem." Sending to CS for review.
josh_cs: Sending to AcmeCorp now. I'll say: we have mitigations in place, expect reduced latency but no systemic errors for most requests, ETA 2hrs for full capacity restoration. If they need immediate SLA credits we'll discuss after triage.
mike_sre: Queue now ~620, error rate 503s down from 12% -> 1.4%. Autoscaler stable for small allocations; large concurrent bursts still see AllocationDenied when trying to allocate >4 GPUs at once.
tara_oncall: Action items captured in bridge notes. Short-term mitigations: routing canary, drained dev pool, reduced batching. Medium-term: request quota increase + explore cross-cloud burst plan. Owner: liam_infra to lead quota request; anya_runtime to follow runtime tuning; mike_sre to monitor.
liam_infra: Opening Azure support ticket (inc# AZ-2026-7891) and submitted quota increase request. Adding case notes: P1, show traffic graphs, ask for expedited review.
incident-bot: Incident bridge created: https://calls.example.com/bridge/7555554321
mike_sre: Monitoring. If we see re-accumulation of queue after draining finished, we'll consider evicting another non-prod pool or increasing canary to 25% temporarily.
tara_oncall: Thanks team. I'll keep the bridge open and post updates. Planning a follow-up postmortem doc once stable. cc @product @cs for customer comms.
josh_cs: Update: AcmeCorp acknowledges receipt. They asked for status updates every 30m — I'll ping with next update in 25m.
mike_sre: Final quick numbers before I sign off from bridge: queue 210, error rate 0.6%, p95 latency back to 950ms. Tracking closely for 30m.
tara_oncall: Marking incident as mitigated for active customer impact; keeping bridge open for monitoring and follow-up. Postmortem owner: tara_oncall. Root cause hypothesis: subscription-level GPU quota + autoscaler burst allocation pattern causing allocation storms; follow-up to include autoscaler retry/backoff tuning and routing safeguards.
emma_product: I'll schedule customer debrief + incident notes for postmortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Closing PAGER (mitigated) — monitoring mode.
